implementation.reason: Explicit selective lazy-import syntax requires Python 3.15; one implementation, no older-runtime fallback.
implementation.validation_contract: One inventory; preflight all executables/batches; format, lint, ty --error all; stop on first failing batch. Fix: lint-fix then format, also fail-fast.
implementation.selection: Per-preflight identities and unique ancestors with directory revalidation; no cross-operation cache; existing byte/snapshot checks retained.
implementation.imports: Selective CLI/handler imports only. Parser discovery remains complete. Global lazy mode never enabled.
implementation.dependency_versions: All 79 locked distribution versions retained; uv regenerated the universal lock for >=3.15.
implementation.larger_refactors: frozendict snapshots, sentinel-based absent/null policies, unpacking comprehensions, parser/handler separation, and validated snapshot reuse require their own contracts and measurements; see CONTRIBUTING.md.

measurement_limits: Synthetic 468-file inventory, actual files/native validators, Git NUL inventory modeled.
Validation fixtures pass both policies; before/after differs deliberately in order, strictness and failure behavior. Timing does not establish failure-workload gains.
Historical 3.14 timing uses original source. Only within-3.15 before/after timings support optimization claims.
Homebrew 3.14/3.15 builds lack JIT. A separately prepared uv-managed 3.15.0 build supports JIT and is evaluated with alternating on/off settings; no cross-build JIT attribution.
3.14 PyYAML includes optional LibYAML; 3.15 source build omits it. Base loader correctness checked; no C-loader gain claimed.
No live LLM, network or transport savings measured; no general consumer replay-speed claim.
reproduction: Reconstruct the unchanged src tree at baseline_revision using read-only git archive/show, outside this checkout; do not retain historical implementations as tests.
